observations: Raw ratio 4/4 inventory items graphical+text; measured graphical totals: 43 svg, 6 meter, 13 badges, 1 role=progressbar (total 63).

Per-service health is triple-encoded: shape-coded SVG glyphs (circle=healthy, triangle=degraded, octagon=down, GLYPH map in source) plus colored text badges 'DOWN'/'DEGRADED'/'HEALTHY' plus colored card left-borders, and repeated as clickable colored segments in the hero strip.
Latency trend on every card is an SVG sparkline (line + area fill + last-point tip circle) with a trend-arrow SVG chip ('▼12%', 'flat'), not just numbers; range text '675–1,311 ms' supports it.
Error-rate trend on every card is an SVG bar chart (barsSVG, 34 buckets, opacity scaled to magnitude) with a trend-arrow chip ('▲22%') and 'peak 63.0%' text support.
Uptime uses a native <meter min=97 max=100 low=99.5 high=99.9> with an SLO tick positioned at 99.9%, alongside the numeric '98.90%' and 'SLO 99.9%' text.

System-level state is also graphical: the hero mini-strip renders one colored segment per service (red/amber/green), and the error/loading states use icon glyphs (alert circle, spinner ring, skeleton cards).
Only 141 visible words for a six-service dashboard (desktop viewportWords=pageWords=141); helperWords 0, longLeafWords 0 — there is not a single explanatory paragraph anywhere.

All real control labels are ≤3 words: 'Refresh', 'Refreshing', 'Live', 'Paused', 'Retry', 'Retry now', 'Copy summary', '1h', '24h', '7d'. The measured labels.maxWords=16 comes from whole service cards being <button> elements whose innerText is the metric grid, not from verbose labels.
Status text is maximally compressed: hero reads '1 down · 1 degraded' with sub '4 healthy of 6 · just now'; header sub is '6 services · 24h window · just now'.
Error copy carries only data: 'Network request failed · NETWORK · attempt 1' and 'auto-retry in 3s' — no apology prose or narration.
Loading sub 'Fetching service metrics' is the longest helper string on the page at three words.
One inconsistency found: the identical immediate-retry action is labeled 'Retry' in the error bar (#ebRetry) but 'Retry now' in the full-page error panel (#pmRetry).
Terminology is otherwise consistent: Down/Degraded/Healthy used identically in badges, hero text, strip tooltips, dialog subtitle, and aria-labels (LABEL map used everywhere).

Copy matches verified behavior: 'auto-retry in Ns' counts down and fires (async item 6), 'Refreshing' appears only while a request is pending (items 2, 10), 'Live'/'Paused' toggle matches the poll state, and 'Copied to clipboard' only after writeText resolves.

No filler, marketing tone, or placeholder text anywhere; even the empty state is a factual 'No services reporting / Nothing registered in this window.' The initial static 'Connecting' sub is overwritten by the first synchronous render() at boot and never user-visible.

The layout is built around the on-call glance: cards are sorted worst-first (sortServices ranks down<degraded<healthy), and the hero computes a single verdict from the worst status ('1 down · 1 degraded', '4 healthy of 6').
Status glyphs are shape-coded (circle/triangle/octagon), so a red/green-colorblind engineer can still read health at a glance — a choice specific to this user.

Operational details no template has: SLO tick at 99.9% on every uptime meter with 'below SLO'/'meets SLO' verdicts in the detail drawer, a 'stale' chip plus 'Refresh failed — showing last known data' that keeps last-known data visible during outages, a status-change chip showing when a service transitioned, an auto-refresh countdown ring, an 'r' keyboard shortcut, and 'Copy summary' producing a paste-ready incident snippet.
Type and color serve the task: JetBrains Mono for all numerics and status text, dark NOC-style theme, red/amber/green mapped strictly to down/degraded/healthy.
Template remnants are minor: the 3-column card grid, Inter for UI chrome, pill-shaped tabs/buttons, and the stock emerald/amber/rose dashboard palette.
Purpose was instantly readable from the idle screenshot: 'Service health · 6 services · 24h window · just now' header over six per-service metric cards — exactly the brief.

What needs attention is unmissable: the red-bordered banner '1 down · 1 degraded' with alert glyph and a red+amber segment strip, and the two problem services (media-worker DOWN, notifier DEGRADED) sorted into the first two positions with red/amber borders and badges.

The primary interactive control (Refresh, top-right, filled-outline button next to the Live indicator and 1h/24h/7d range tabs) was obvious; the page correctly makes reading status, not clicking, the primary act for an on-call engineer.
All three pre-source answers checked out against the brief and the source with no corrections needed.
